facts.text: The default image width and height are 200 pixels
The wrist rotations are 0, 30, 60, 90, -30 and -60 degrees, indexed 0 to 5
The action space is MultiDiscrete([IMAGE_HEIGHT * IMAGE_WIDTH, len(rotations)])
An action is decoded as x = action[0] % IMAGE_WIDTH, y = action[0] // IMAGE_WIDTH and rotation = action[1]
The environment steps MuJoCo with frame_skip 1
The default scene's MuJoCo integration timestep is 2e-3 s
An observation is a dictionary with an rgb array and a depth array returned by the controller's camera
get_observation requests an IMAGE_WIDTH by IMAGE_HEIGHT image and converts the depth image to meters
The reward is binary: 0 when the pixel is skipped or the grasp fails, and 1 when move_and_grasp reports a grasp
A pixel whose projected world z is below 0.8 m or whose world y is above -0.3 m is skipped with reward 0
step always returns done False and an empty info dictionary, and increments step_called
reset_model is called by the parent class reset method and returns an observation image
reset_model sets the seven actuated joints to [0, -1.57, 1.57, -1.57, -1.57, 0.0, 0.3]
reset_model randomizes 40 object joints: x in [-0.25, 0.25], y in [-0.77, -0.43], z in [1.0, 1.5] and a random unit quaternion
Grasper-v0 is registered with entry point gym_grasper.envs:GraspEnv
close closes the MuJoCo environment and destroys the OpenCV windows
The README documents the default action space as 200 x 200 pixels (40000 choices) and the state as a dictionary with an RGB image and a depth image of that resolution

determinism.notes: reset(seed) and cap.world.seed.v1 fix the fake's occupancy grid and the fake is otherwise deterministic, so the same seed and actions repeat a trajectory; upstream draws the 40 object poses with numpy's global generator and Quaternion.random (GraspingEnv.py:426-430), so a seed does not give the same scene on the two

gaps: analytic F0 stand-in: no MuJoCo, no rigid-body dynamics, no contacts, friction, actuators, sensors or the 40-object pile; the reward only marks a pixel of the fake's occupancy grid and ignores every controller result
the fake returns 8 x 8 RGB and depth arrays where the upstream camera returns the default 200 x 200 x 3 and 200 x 200 arrays (GraspingEnv.py:31-32); the observation space advertises the real shapes
no rendering, camera image, inverse kinematics, controller, move_and_grasp or wrist rotation motion; the fake's occupancy grid, density and colours are test data, marked placeholder in fake.py
the upstream environment is legacy gym with mujoco_py and returns a 4-tuple from step (GraspingEnv.py:156); the fake follows that 4-tuple and returns the reset observation without an info dictionary
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, a tick is one step() call and the 2 ms timestep is the upstream MuJoCo timestep, not a measured duration
the fake was never compared with the upstream environment or with a UR5 and gripper; nothing was validated on hardware
reset options are accepted for the Gymnasium bridge and ignored: the upstream reset_model reads no options (GraspingEnv.py:409-477)
snapshot and restore are not offered: the fake exposes no get_state or set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
